# 1 Clement Chapter 36 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_036_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 36

**36:1** This is the way, beloved, in which we found our salvation: Jesus Christ, the high priest of our offerings, the guardian and champion of our weakness.

**36:2** Through him we gaze intently into the heights of heaven; through him we behold as in a mirror his blameless and most exalted face; through him the eyes of our heart have been opened; through him our foolish and darkened mind blooms toward the wonderful light of his knowledge; through him the Lord has willed that we should taste immortal knowledge — he who is "the radiance of his glory and the very stamp of his being, upholding all things by the word of his power" — at whose right hand the angels and archangels and powers and thrones and dominions are set in array, giving worship.

**36:3** Through the immensity and excellence of his beauty the six-winged and many-eyed ones stand before him — the seraphim and the cherubim — crying: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole creation is full of his glory."

**36:4** And we too, gathered together in concord in one place, should cry out earnestly to him as from one mouth, that we may become partakers of his great and glorious promises.

**36:5** For it says: "Eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and into the heart of man it has not arisen, the things which he has prepared for those who wait for him."

---

*LOGOS preserves the anaphoric structure of v. 2 ("through him... through him... through him...") which mirrors the style of Hebrews 1. The Hebrews 1:3 citation is rendered in close parallel to its source.*
